recipes.name: Fresh Ginger Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1.25 cups white sugar, divided, or more to taste

steps.text: Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Beat 1 cup sugar, butter, and ginger in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Beat in molasses and egg. Gently fold in flour mixture until just combined. Chill for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Roll chilled dough into 1 1/2 inch balls. Roll balls in remaining sugar, then place 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets.

Bake in the preheated oven until mostly (but not fully) set in the centers and edges are starting to brown, about 15 minutes. Let stand for 1 minute on the baking sheets, then remove to wire racks and let cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Fresh Ginger Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Fresh ginger cookies are somewhere between a molasses cookie and a gingersnap. Chewy and flavorful, they're perfect for your next holiday cookie swap.

review.reviewBody:
I was looking for something like the chewy ginger-molasses cookies at Starbucks, and this recipe does the trick. Thank you!

By the way, fresh ginger grates much easier if you freeze it first, and then use a microplane grater.

I love these cookies! I have made this recipe about 20 times, so I thought I would share my tips.

1) I use dry ginger, but otherwise follow the recipe to the letter. 

2) Don't add all the flour mixture at once. Sometimes it doesn't need it all and the dough will be too dry. 

3) The dough, when completed, should be uniform in colour and texture. You should be able to pick it up with your hands and form it into a large ball without any cracks. It should also not stick to your fingers.

4) Chilling the dough is paramount. If the dough is not chilled enough, then the cookies will be too flat, won't form a crispy crust, and won't have the awesome cracks on the top.

5) I use a 1/8 cup measuring thingy to make all my dough balls exactly the same size (crazy?). They cook for exactly 15 minutes at 350 in my oven. The middle of each cookie will be raised, but will fall when it cools.

6)I prefer them a couple days old, but my G/F likes then best right from the oven.

I want to add some more detail on the look of the cookie. Using a 1/8 cup ball, and cooking for 15 minutes, I get a cookie that is just over 1cm thick. Every cookie has deep cracks (deeper than the picture). I sprinkle sugar on them when they come out of the oven too.

If you cookie is too flat and lacks cracks, your dough was either too wet, or you didn't chill the dough enough. 

If the cookie has a rounded, puffy top, and the cookie tastes dry, then the dough had too much flour added to it.

Good luck!

Followed the recipe exactly as written and they came out perfect. On the second batch I baked them for 12 minutes to get them even softer. The only thing I noticed was how much the flavors mellowed after a day. To get that just out of the oven taste I just warmed them in a low oven for a few minutes. They also make a wonderful substitution for graham crackers for a cookie crust. I use just enough melted butter to keep the crumbs together. I have also used them in my peach crisp recipe.

I rarely give a recipe 5 stars but I would give these AMAZING cookies 10 stars if I could! I cut the fresh ginger to 1 Tbl. as I thought 2 Tbl. would be too strong for my taste. I used salted butter so could cut added salt to 1/8 tsp, or not. I needed less than 1/4 c. sugar to roll the dough balls in. Don't flatten the dough balls on the cookie sheet. I baked them about 10 minutes. This made 43 cookies with my cookie scoop. I've made these 3 times and I'm sure I'll be making them again!

These were awesome!! The only things I changed was that I used whole wheat pastry flour instead of white flour, I didn't roll in sugar and I put dough in freezer for about 10 minutes instead of in refrigerator for an hour.
My wife loves these cookies... Not overly sweet I use a micro plane and double up the fresh ginger.

Delish! In addition to chopped ginger, I also used a garlic press to crush ginger for the juice (keep the juice, find something else to do with the pulp). Added a 1/4-ish tsp of chipotle pepper for a little kick. Last, I also added crushed ginger to the sugar coating.
Every one o have made it for. Absolutely loved it. I did add teaspoon of all spice in it..

Wonderful cookies! I didn't have any molasses, so I substituted Steen's Cane Syrup. Grating the the ginger for the first batch was the hardest part. The second time I made the cookies, I used minced garlic in a jar found in the produce section of the grocery store next to the minced garlic. Using the minced ginger simplified the process! Lots less time and frustration! However, I discovered after the cookies were baked that minced ginger requires quite a bit more ginger than grated ginger to achieve the same spicy flavor. I will use lots more minced ginger next time.

I made a Gluten Free version, using the same measurements cup for cup with Red Mills' All Purpose Gluten Free Flour. I added 1/4 tsp xantham gum. I also subbed two heaping Tbl of powdered ginger for the fresh and the cookies were amazing! So easy! I should've been making these for years.

These were really easy to make. I love ginger cookies that have a good ginger punch to them. I used ground ginger but next time I will use fresh ginger. I think this will give more flavor..I used brown sugar instead of white, I also added 1/2 tsp cloves and 1 tsp of cinnamon. They turned out great. Very soft and chewy. I will be making these again but with real ginger. ?
made with 2T ground ginger instead, everything else as is. made 24 delicious cookies with a perfect bite. delicious!

These cookies are very moreish! I don’t imagine they’ll survive more than a day in our household! One thing I’ll say is that 1.5-inch balls with this amount of dough will only yield about 20 cookies, rather than 30, but I can’t fault them otherwise. They’re chewy and gingery and so delicious. My husband compares the flavour to candied ginger and I agree. So tasty and easy to make, so this one is definitely a keeper!

The first time I made these cookies, I followed the recipe to a T but I forgot to chill the dough. The cookies still turned out OK, but they were far too sweet for my tastes. I just made them again. I cut the amount of sugar by more than half and they were far better. They're still sweet and I can't imagine anyone thinking they could use more sugar. Instead of using 1 1/4 cup of sugar as specified in the recipe, I used 1/2 cup. I suggest everyone give it a try.
I added cinnamon and cloves too! Sooo good!
I made these without sugar just honey and molasses came out really good

I made two variations of these and both were spectacular! First I did a ginger and molasses variation (following the recipe) then I did another which used honey instead of molasses and added lemon in addition to ginger, both versions were highly favored amongst friends a family! A delightful recipe with some nice room for experimentation.
I have made this recipe 4 times. Every time they have come out awesome .I love the flavor the real ginger gives the cookies. 10 out of 10 I highly recommend!
15 minutes was a bit too long in my oven but otherwise, I loved these. Easy, fast. I refrigerated these in a bag, flattened, and cut into squares to bake.
I Use this recipe all the time , the best 👍, I’m wondering if this recipe could work for cut out cookies ? Gingerbread men in particular
